tasks.title: Implement core chat server
tasks.description: Create a TCP server that accepts connections, enforces unique nicknames, broadcasts messages, and announces joins/leaves.
acceptance_criteria: R1: The server must accept at least 10 clients connected at the same time.
R2: Each client must choose a unique nickname when it connects.
R3: A message sent by one client must be delivered to every other connected client.
R4: The server shall announce when a client joins or leaves the chat.
R7: The server must not crash when a client disconnects without warning.

tasks.title: Add private messaging command
tasks.description: Extend the server to parse the /msg command and deliver a private message to the specified recipient.
acceptance_criteria: R5: Clients should be able to send a private message with the command /msg.

tasks.title: Test connection capacity and latency
tasks.description: Run load tests with 10+ simulated clients and measure message delivery time to ensure it is under one second.
acceptance_criteria: R1: The server must accept at least 10 clients connected at the same time.
R8: Messages should reach other clients within one second on a local network.

tasks.title: Test server robustness on abrupt disconnects
tasks.description: Simulate unexpected client terminations and verify the server remains stable.
acceptance_criteria: R7: The server must not crash when a client disconnects without warning.

tasks.title: Implement message history buffer
tasks.description: Store the last 50 broadcast messages and send them to newly connected clients.
acceptance_criteria: R6: The server may keep a history of the last 50 messages for new clients.

roadmap.markdown:
# Plan

12 steps, about 39 hours of work; with enough agents working in parallel the longest chain (critical path) takes 26 hours over 8 stages.

## Research

- **research** Research the approach (research.run, 2 h, high) **(critical)**
- **verify** Check the research findings (verify.claims, 1 h, high) — after research **(critical)**

## Design

- **design** Design the solution (code.implement, 2 h, high) — after verify **(critical)**

## Build

- *Core*
  - **T1** Implement core chat server (code.implement, 8 h, urgent) [R1, R2, R3, R4, R7] — after design **(critical)**
- *Messaging*
  - **T2** Add private messaging command (code.implement, 4 h, high) [R5] — after T1 **(critical)**
- *History*
  - **T3** Implement message history buffer (code.implement, 3 h, low) [R6] — after T1

## Test

- **T4** Test connection capacity and latency (test.run, 5 h, high) [R1, R8] — after T1
- **T5** Validate core and private messaging functionality (test.run, 6 h, urgent) [R2, R3, R4, R5, R6] — after T2, T3 **(critical)**
- **T6** Test server robustness on abrupt disconnects (test.run, 3 h, high) [R7] — after T1

## Document

- **T7** Prepare README (docs.generate, 2 h, high) — after T4, T5, T6 **(critical)**
- **T8** Prepare Design report (docs.generate, 2 h, normal) — after T4, T5, T6

## Review

- **review** Final review (review.final, 1 h, high) — after T7, T8 **(critical)**

## Critical path

research (Research the approach) -> verify (Check the research findings) -> design (Design the solution) -> T1 (Implement core chat server) -> T2 (Add private messaging command) -> T5 (Validate core and private messaging functionality) -> T7 (Prepare README) -> review (Final review)

## Stages (steps in one stage can run at the same time)

1. research
2. verify
3. design
4. T1
5. T2, T3, T4, T6
6. T5
7. T7, T8
8. review
